item.title: Momiji Manju: Miyajima's Maple-Leaf Cakes — Guide
item.description: Momiji manju are little cakes baked in the shape of a maple leaf, a nod to the maples of Momijidani, and they are the definitive souvenir of Hiroshima. Created on Miyajima over a century ago, they are made from a light castella-style sponge batter poured into leaf-shaped moulds and filled traditionally with sweet red bean paste, though modern fillings run to custard, chocolate, matcha and cheese. On Miyajima you can watch them being made on rotating griddles and eat them still warm, which is a completely different experience from the boxed ones — and several shops sell them battered and deep-fried on a stick as age-momiji.
